question: Since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine and the EU’s decision to impose sanctions on Russia and price caps on Russian oil, a shadow fleet has appeared. It consists of a growing number of older vessels with unclear ownership and is being used to circumvent the sanctions.

Recently, Sveriges Television reported that the Cyprus-registered oil tanker Zircone had docked off the coast of Gotland and was refuelling vessels from the Russian shadow fleet. The activities of the Russian shadow fleet in the Baltic Sea pose major economic, ecological and security political risks. 1.
What steps will the Commission take to manage the economic, ecological and security policy risks linked to the presence of the shadow fleet in the Baltic Sea?
What measures will the Commission take, within the framework of the EU’s cooperation with the International Maritime Organization, to prevent and limit the activities of the shadow fleet?
How can the Commission act to ensure that all vessels navigating in EU waters are insured and meet high environmental standards so as to prevent accidents?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (7.6.2024) Russia is using a shadow fleet of older tankers to transport its oil in an effort to circumvent EU sanctions and the Group of Seven Plus (G7+) oil price cap. The Commission takes seriously the environmental and maritime safety risks posed by the dark fleet used by Russia to transport its oil.

It is engaging at international level, including through the International Maritime Organization (IMO) and the International Oil Pollution Compensation Funds (IOPC Funds). The Commission and Member States worked together for the adoption of the ‘dark fleet’ resolution at the IMO in December 2023, which defines, for the first time, the dark fleet and sets out recommendations for coastal and flag states1.

The Commission is also working on measures to prevent unlawful practices associated with the fraudulent registration and fraudulent registries of vessels. EU sanctions are kept under constant review and can be expanded to achieve their objectives and address relevant challenges, including circumvention by nefarious actors involved in the shadow fleet.
All EU restrictive measures are agreed by unanimity in the Council.
